name: Modulatricidae
description: Modulatricidae is a small family of African passerine birds with uncertain taxonomic history. They were formerly placed with thrushes and babblers but are now recognized as a distinct lineage.

children.name: Modulatrix
children.description: A monotypic genus of thrush-like bird found in montane forests of eastern Africa.

children.name: Modulatrix stictigula
children.description:
The spot-throat (Modulatrix stictigula) is a species of bird in the family Modulatricidae. It is the only member of the genus Modulatrix. It is native to the Eastern Arc forests.
This species is monotypic, although it was previously thought to have two subspecies.

children.name: Arcanator
children.description: A genus of two species of shy, thrush-like birds found in African montane forests.

children.name: Arcanator orostruthus
children.description:
The dapple-throat (Arcanator orostruthus) is a species of bird in the small African family Modulatricidae. Other common names include dappled mountain robin and dappled mountain greenbul. It is native to Mozambique and Tanzania. This is the only species in the monotypic genus Arcanator.
This species has a disjunct distribution, occurring in a few mountain ranges, including the Usambara and Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania and the Njesi Highlands and Mount Mabu in northern Mozambique. It lives in dense, wet mountain forest habitat. It can be found in the leaf litter near streams, where it seeks insects.

children.name: Arcanator nigriceps
children.description: The Dusky Greenbul is a dark olive-brown bird with a blackish crown and pale eyes. It inhabits montane forests in the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania.

children.name: Kakamega poliothorax
children.description: Kakamega poliothorax (Grey-chested Babbler) is a modulatricidae species found in its native region.
